item.title: Fly fishing, Stanley, Idaho!
item.description: I’m heading up to Stanley this weekend and I’ve never fished up there. There’s not much info online, but I was curious if anybody has experience fishing the Salmon up that way. I’m not asking for specific spots or holes, just curious how the fishing is downstream of town, or if I should spend my time upstream instead.

item.title: 3rd Time’s a Charm
item.description: Caught near St. Simon Island, in South Georgia. This was my third trip looking for redfish, the prior 2 trips we didn’t so much a see a single fin, and the fish did not disappoint. Saltwater fly fishing is absurdly fun.

item.title: Catching a Redfish in a Puddle?
item.description: A Note from @maketimeforfishing: “I was kayaking a small creek in Charleston when it got too shallow, so I ditched the kayak and started wading. Around the next bend, I found fish tailing, waking, and blowing up on bait everywhere.

item.title: Lowcountry Winter Redfish
item.description: By Owen Plair What makes the winter fishing for redfish so special? There are not many fisheries that have a winter time season, due to migratory fish, cold temps, snow, and ice. One of the many great things about the Lowcountry is that it is a year round fishery for Redfish.

item.title: Rob Smith’s Rusty Enema
item.description: THE STASH IS BACK! Rob “The Stash” Smith is back to share one of his favorite redfish flies with us. The Rusty Enema is a proven producer anywhere redfish are found. It’s a great attractor pattern that pushes a lot of water, which is like ringing the dinner bell for redfish in dirty water.

item.title: Chokoloskee Trip
item.description: Last weekend went on a tarpon trip ended up with Redfish and snook started the trip out with Captin Taylor Schaeffer ran outside. We posted it up with his mourning bouy , but the water was too cold. Tarpon were acting weird. I was hoping to use the new one piece Hardy I picked up from Ole Florida Fly Shop but unfortunately nothing wanted to play.

item.title: A Year Fishing The Everglades Special, Half Way Through A Bad Decision
item.description: By Paul Pucket FISHING WISE, I HAVE NEVER HAD A YEAR LIKE THIS ONE. I am fishing in places I have never fished and feel very lucky to have the opportunities. The main difference between this year, and the prior years spent chasing these mindless, slimy, instinctual creatures, is that I am limited to one fly. All year. The Everglades Special.

item.title: Shoutout to the boat dogs. I just lost my net-man of 12 years 🎣
item.description: Tucker, named after the Tuckaseegee River in western North Carolina, floated many streams and kissed many fishes in his 12 years with me. He’s seen everything from tailing redfish in South Carolina, smallmouth in Ohio, tiger trout in Utah, brown trout in Montana, even the elusive bull trout in Oregon.

item.title: Last Cast Bonefish
item.description: Bonefishing, for me, is the purest form of the drug. I’m just returning from the first of three G&G Bonefish Schools in the Bahamas. This trip was more of a reunion than a school, with better than half of the anglers returning for the second or third time.
